Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 34924 of 2023

Applicant :- Anil
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Lal Prabhakar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State apprised the Court that on 30.07.2023 notice has been served to the informant of the case.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

2. Heard Sri Lal Prabhakar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
3.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
110 of 2023, under Sections 363, 376 IPC & 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Asmauli, District- Sambhal, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
4. FIR of the present case was lodged against unknown person under Section 363 IPC and according to the FIR, some unknown person enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 15 years.

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant was not named in the FIR but duing investigation when prosecutrix was recovered and her statement was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. then she stated that she is sixteen and half years' old and applicant has enticed her away and also forcibly made physical relationship with her but when her statement was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then she categorically stated that she had gone along with the applicant according to her own wish and she loved the applicant for last three years and also performed marriage with him, therefore, from the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., consent of the prosecutrix is quite apparent.
6.

He further submitted that although, as per the school record, at the time of incident prosecutrix was around sixteen and half years' old but during investigation her ossification test was not conducted and in fact she is major girl and applicant and prosecutrix both loved each other,
therefore, it is a case of love-affair and it appears that her wrong date of birth has been mentioned in the school record.
7. He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal and he is in jail since 21.06.2023.

8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that as per the school record,
prosecutrix is hardly sixteen and half years' old and therefore, her consent is immaterial.
9. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. Although, as per the school record, prosecutrix appears to be sixteen and half years' old girl at the time of incident and in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she made allegation of enticement against the applicant and also stated that he forcibly made physical relationship with her but when her statement was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then she stated that she loved the applicant for three years and she had gone along with him according to her own wish and also performed marriage with him, therefore, from her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it appears that it is a case of love-affair and prosecutrix was consenting party.
11. Admittedly, during investigation, ossification test of the prosecutrix was not conducted.
12. Law is settled that bail application should not be dismissed either for punitive or for preventive purposes.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant- Anil be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
